body.statement:
For every \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\), there is a universal \(C>0\) such that \(\mathsf A(G,T,e,\delta)\) returns, with total symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\), exactly one of the following tags. If \(d_e(G)<\infty\), it returns
\[
(\operatorname{algebraic},\mathcal J_{G,e},2^{|D|-n+2}),
\]
where \(\mathcal J_{G,e}\) is a Jacobian-rank transcript certifying algebraicity and
\[
d_e(G)\leq 2^{|D|-n+2}\leq 2^{k+1}.
\]
If \(d_e(G)=\infty\), it returns exactly \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\), where \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) certifies that the queried-coordinate projection of the integral generic fiber is dominant onto \(\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\). In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), its construction time and certificate length are at most \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\). The algebraic tag does not claim to compute \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\).
body.justification: The unconditional operational result is an exact algebraic-versus-transcendental tag with a certified finite-degree ceiling; it no longer launders an absent eliminant.
body.gap: Neither general polynomial-space identification nor extensional quadratic-core reduction constructs the bounded source-prime chart needed for exact finite output.
body.consumer: fasttreeid can safely report finite algebraic ambiguity versus an infinite queried projection; exact degree and polynomial output require the conditional chart theorem.
body.proof_tex:
Put
\[
u=(\lambda_D,\omega_B,\omega_{\mathrm{diag}})
\quad\text{and}\quad
N=|D|+|B|+n,
\]
so that \(L=\mathbb C(u_1,\ldots,u_N)\). Choose a topological ordering of the acyclic directed graph. In that ordering \(\Lambda^n=0\), and therefore
\[
(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}=I_n+\Lambda+\cdots+\Lambda^{n-1}.
\]
Thus each distinct covariance entry
\[
s_{ij}(u)=\phi_G(\sigma_{ij})
=\bigl[(I_n-\Lambda)^{-\mathsf T}\Omega(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}\bigr]_{ij}
\]
is a polynomial of total degree at most \(2n-1\), represented by an arithmetic circuit of size polynomial in \(n\). Let \(s=(s_{ij}:i\leq j)\), let \(J_0=\partial s/\partial u\), and let \(J_1\) be obtained from \(J_0\) by adjoining the row \(\partial\lambda_e/\partial u\). All entries of these matrices have degree at most \(2n-2\).

We first prove the field-theoretic rank criterion used by the algorithm. Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in L\), and choose a transcendence basis \(b_1,\ldots,b_r\) of \(\mathbb C(a_1,\ldots,a_m)/\mathbb C\) from among a maximal algebraically independent subfamily of the \(a_i\). Extend it to a transcendence basis \(b_1,\ldots,b_r,c_1,\ldots,c_q\) of \(L/\mathbb C\). The extension
\[
L/\mathbb C(b_1,\ldots,b_r,c_1,\ldots,c_q)
\]
is algebraic and separable because the characteristic is zero. The coordinate derivations with respect to the \(b_j\) extend uniquely through a separable algebraic extension: if \(v\) has minimal polynomial \(g\), differentiating \(g(v)=0\) gives
\[
g'(v)\,dv=-\sum_{ell}v^\ell\,d g_\ell,
\]
and \(g'(v)\neq0\). Applying these extended derivations to a relation \(\sum_j q_j,db_j=0\), with \(q_j\in L\), gives \(q_j=0\) for each \(j\). Hence \(db_1,\ldots,db_r\) are linearly independent over \(L\). Conversely, each \(a_i\) is algebraic over \(\mathbb C(b_1,\ldots,b_r)\); differentiating its separable minimal polynomial expresses \(da_i\) in the \(L\)-span of \(db_1,\ldots,db_r\). Consequently
\[
\dim_L\operatorname{span}_L\{da_1,\ldots,da_m\}
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C(a_1,\ldots,a_m).
\]

Apply this identity first to the covariance polynomials and then to the covariance polynomials together with \(\lambda_e\). Since the rows of their Jacobians are the coordinate vectors of the corresponding differentials in the basis \(du_1,\ldots,du_N\),
\[
\operatorname{rank}_L J_0=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G,
\qquad
\operatorname{rank}_L J_1=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G(\lambda_e).
\]
Adjoining one element raises transcendence degree by either zero or one. Therefore
\[
\operatorname{rank}_LJ_1=\operatorname{rank}_LJ_0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\lambda_e\text{ is algebraic over }K_G,
\]
whereas a rank increase by one is equivalent to transcendence.

The two generic ranks are obtained by evaluating \(J_0\) and \(J_1\) at one random source point and performing exact Gaussian elimination. Both matrices have at most \(N+1\leq n^2+1\) rows or columns. A nonzero maximal minor has total degree at most
\[
(n^2+1)(2n-2)\leq 2n^3.
\]
Choose the source coordinates independently and uniformly from a finite subset of \(\mathbb Q\) of cardinality at least \(8n^3/\delta\). An evaluated rank can never exceed the generic rank. If it is smaller, a fixed nonzero maximal minor vanished at the chosen point. By \(\mathrm{lem:schwartz\mbox{-}zippel\mbox{-}bound}\), this has probability at most \(\delta/4\) for each of \(J_0\) and \(J_1\). Allowing the remaining \(\delta/2\) budget for the source identity tests recorded in the transcript and applying the union bound gives total symbolic error at most \(\delta\). On the complementary event, equality or a one-rank increase gives the correct tag by the displayed rank criterion. The exact evaluation point, pivot positions, and pivot minors form \(\mathcal J_{G,e}\).

Suppose that the augmented rank is larger. Then \(\lambda_e\) is transcendental over \(K_G\), so the homomorphism
\[
K_G[t]\longrightarrow A_K,
\qquad t\longmapsto\lambda_e,
\]
is injective. Because \(A_K\) is integral by \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\), the induced morphism \(\operatorname{Spec}(A_K)\to\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\) is dominant. Its domain has positive relative dimension, since its fraction field \(L\) contains an element transcendental over \(K_G\). The nonzero augmented pivot minor together with the two rank transcripts is therefore the claimed source-parametric dominance certificate \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\).

On the equality branch, \(d_e(G)<\infty\), and the already established \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\) gives
\[
d_e(G)\leq2^{|D|-n+2}\leq2^{k+1}.
\]
It supplies an upper bound only; no multiplication algebra or eliminant has been constructed.

The nilpotent matrix sum, circuit differentiation, exact evaluations, and Gaussian eliminations use a number of arithmetic operations and transcript entries polynomial in \(n\); the random sampling needs \(O(\log(1/\delta)+\log n)\) bits per coordinate, whose bit cost is charged separately in \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\). Since \(n\geq2\) and \(k\geq0\), a fixed polynomial in \(n\) is bounded by \(n^{C(k+1)}\) for a universal \(C\). This proves the stated time, length, and error guarantees, as well as the explicit absence of \(p_e\)-dependent outputs on the algebraic tag.
